Definition: prolongation from G1364; double, i.e. twin; Didymus, a Christian:--Didymus.
BiblicalUsage: Didymus is the name the Gospels give Thomas, the Twin, and it stands three times, always beside his name. He speaks up to go and die with Jesus, he doubts until he sees, and he is there at the lake when the risen Lord appears.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Thomas the Twin is the apostle for every doubter. He asked to see, he touched, and he confessed My Lord and my God, and his doubt became the clearest confession in the Gospels.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
